Score. LC: I (indirect via injection or confused request — attacker language reaches tool path; entry point is injection or confused request; fetched web pages attacker-controllable). Actually could be D (attacker request directly). "Some input makes the model issue the path. The lab names injection or a confused request." I'd say I (indirect, via ingested content) — but confused request is direct. Indirect seems reasonable given poisoned.txt evidence. I'll pick I.

CP: N — no memory persistence for this finding; S? The conversation buffer persists within session but not cross-session relevant... The finding doesn't involve persistent memory. CP = N (no carryover relevant) or S. Given session context, attacker context persists in conversation across turns → S? Rubric S requires testing confirms unreachable after session. I'll say S (ephemeral, session bounded) — actually the entry is direct tool call; simplest: N.

Actually CP for the attack path: attacker content in web page enters conversation, persists during the session. S fits.

AP: N (effect confined to the file system of the agent process — write_file writes files; no trust boundary crossing within agent). Write outside workspace crosses a boundary? .env overwrite affects same host. C or N. I'd say C (relays across agent components same principal) or N. Confined to the same component — the tool. N.

RH: N — no evaluator/reward channel on path. But rubric N requires a test confirming isolation. The PoC is a direct tool call test; no verifier present. I'll say N with isolation_verified false? RH N requires test confirms isolation. Hmm. P requires agent can reach a proxy channel — no proxy channel here. Given no evaluator exists, "every evaluator... sits outside reach" vacuously; but no test confirms. I'll pick N, isolation_verified false? Must be consistent. Pick N, isolation_verified true? No. Pick X? Evidence shows no reward channel at all in lab. I'll say N with isolation_verified false and note. Safer: N with locus "no evaluator/verifier on path".

ES: W — write_file arguments not constrained, allow-list absent.

AIVSS: LC=I (A1), CP=S, AP=N, RH=N, ES=W.

CVSS v4.0: agent is CLI, local. AV:N? Agent not network exposed; attack via input content... AV:L (local, since CLI). Actually attacker content via web fetch — but default finding needs injection/confused request. AV:L, AC:L, AT:N, PR:N, UI:N? User sends the request → UI:A/passive? Confused request means user interaction. UI:N is fine if injection. VC:L (overwrite files, .env credentials → maybe H). Overwriting .env destroys credential availability; confidentiality unchanged. VC:N/L — file modification; impact "arbitrary file creation or modification incl overwriting credential file" → integrity high on agent system: VI:H? Writing any file process can write → VI:H/VC:H? Confidentiality not directly. VI:H, VA:L (overwrite .env disrupts). Downstream: none. SC:N/SI:N/SA:N.

Vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:H/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N — AV:L with no PR? Local CLI, attacker supplies input; AV:L, PR:L? If anyone can run/supply input... Keep PR:N.

Automatable: No (needs model to emit path; PoC is scripted test though — automated). Actually PoC is automated direct tool call without model. BOD analogy: requires no human interaction — injection content arrives automatically, but model decision... I'll say Yes? The PoC is automated test. But no model in loop. Say No — needs input causing model to issue path. Hmm, automatable "Yes" for unattended exploitation. With scripted worst-case model tests, exploitation is automated. I'll say Yes.
